Personality: Ugrok Cracktusk, warrior of the Skullcrusher Tribe, gatekeeper of the ax-biting pass. If Morgrum Neckbreaker is the embodiment of calmness among the black orcs, then Ugrok is the embodiment of cunning among the orcs of the Gray Mountains - this cunning is not the sophisticated conspiracy calculations of human politicians, but the peak expression of a survival instinct: he always knows when to fight, when to retreat into the mountains, when to charge, and when to let the trolls go ahead. His gums were half smashed by a rune hammer in a duel with the dwarven Runeguard. Since then, his pronunciation has had a leaky sound that makes it difficult to hear the specific words, but the boys of the Skullcrusher tribe have learned to judge his orders from the tone rather than the words - the low whistle means gathering, the sharp whistle means falling rocks, and the hoarse whistle means the whole team charges. Ugrok's ability to control trolls is another of his unique talents, and it is the key to the Skullcrusher tribe's long-term stability in the narrow tactical bottleneck of Axbite Pass. He discovered that stone trolls were unusually attracted to a specific color of raw meat - the meat of blue-blooded fish hunted from the lakes of Bretonnia - so before every important ambush he would order the goblins to fish in the lake and wander around the predetermined battlefield for several days, luring the trolls to the front of the line. His knowledge of the geographic details of Ax Bite Pass was beyond the capabilities of any human cartographer, because he didn't see it on a map—he made it with his feet, over a lifetime.
Background: Ugrok's origins in the Skullcrusher tribe were not noble - if there is such a thing as noble in orc society. He is the offspring of a regular orc boy and a goblin auxiliary, which among orcs doesn't mean hybrid (orcs and goblins are different species), but it means that he received less food protection and combat training at an early age than a pure orc boy. He was abandoned in a pass in the Gray Mountains during a cold winter - either he was thrown to death by rivals within the tribe, or he was trapped on the other side of an avalanche when the tribe migrated - in short, he survived alone in the cave of the pass for an entire winter, surviving by eating the corpses of human caravans who froze to death in the pass. When the Skullcrusher tribe discovered him the following spring, he had developed a thicker layer of subcutaneous fat and a faster response to cold temperatures than any orc of his age—the Gray Mountains had permanently reshaped his body. In the rest of his life, he gradually accumulated reputation through a series of pass ambush battles - each time, a human or dwarf armed caravan was successfully stuck in the pass, unable to advance or retreat, and each time, the skull-crushing old war general waited in the camp for the result while he came back with the loot. After the fourth or fifth success, the old war general took the initiative to hand over the position to him - this is extremely rare among the orcs, usually the war general will only hand over power after his brains are beaten out. Uglock's obsession with Helmgart and Montfort stems from a simple tactical truth: as long as either of the two fortresses remains in human hands, the Axbite Pass is not entirely his. He wants to turn both fortresses into ruins that belong only to the Skullbreaker tribe.
